names.name: Maple bar
names.said: On the West Coast it is a bar. Say Long John in Portland and you will be understood, and marked.

text.what: A bar of raised dough, fried, then topped end to end with maple-flavoured icing. Sometimes filled with custard or cream; sometimes finished with chopped bacon, which is a newer idea and an argued one.
text.story: The same pastry carries different names by region. Long John runs through the Midwest, Canada and Texas; the Mid-Atlantic and central Canada sometimes sell it as an éclair, though an éclair is choux and this is yeast; parts of the Midwest say finger doughnut or cream stick when it is filled. On the West Coast it is a bar — maple bar, chocolate bar, filled bar — and the maple one is the one the coast is known for.
text.how: Sheet raised dough, cut rectangles, proof, fry, cool enough that icing will not run off, then dip the top face in maple icing and set it down icing-up.
text.today: A maple bar is the default second donut in a West Coast dozen — the one that goes in after the glazed.
